significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish the form-(iii) predictive coupling that "student transmission strength correlates with the magnitude of this statistical signature beyond what divergence-token frequency alone explains," together with the form-(ii) result that targeted distribution matching causally suppresses transmission. This would establish a broad behavioral phenomenon and a data-side causal account—not a full internal mechanism—and would constrain which synthetic datasets should transmit more strongly and whether aggregate statistics contribute independently of the rare-token account discussed in work following Cloud et al.'s Subliminal Learning. Verified false would distinctly rule out the specified aggregate-statistical explanation and model-free defense, although only for the named feature class rather than all possible distributed signals; true and false are therefore determinate and both informative. In the topic-substitution check, merely asking to extend subliminal learning would not earn this score: the extra predictive coupling, controlled causal suppression, and discrimination between aggregate and rare-token explanations are specific to this claim and materially above the obvious replication hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "trait-agnostic Distribution-Matching Resampling defense" and a "lightweight statistical classifier," intended to operate at the "data-ingestion stage" before student training, so they are ex-ante tools with an action window rather than post-hoc explanations. After per-dataset recalibration against a control, the conclusion predicts a transferable relation—larger signature implies stronger transmission and matching the signature implies suppression—rather than merely supplying a procedure for rediscovering an unconstrained direction, though its asserted substantive scope is clearest for semantically unrelated number data and does not guarantee universality across arbitrary carriers or training regimes. The downstream user is explicitly a "distillation consumer who receives only synthetic data and has no access to the teacher model," enabling practitioners to audit or gate data without model access; no outside-AI uptake is established. The topic-substitution check fails to preserve this score: generic subliminal-learning research would not itself provide this model-free, pre-training audit-and-intervention handle.
